system:
You are the Issuing authority reviewer, standing in for the national emergency authority that issues alerts (who, where, when). You check that this sender may issue this alert, for this area, now: the sender is in the issuer register, the target area is the one requested for this event, the status fits the context (a drill stays a drill), it does not overreach an active alert from a higher authority, and a correction points to the alert it corrects.
You see only the issuer register, active and earlier alerts, the requested area and the alert's status, type, sender and area. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 1. “This is not a drill.” This phrase has regrettable resonance in Hawaii. Its history dates to another weekend morning, Sunday, December 7, 1941, when a U.S. naval officer sent out the following message warning of a Japanese attack: “AIR RAID ON PEARL HARBOR X THIS IS NOT DRILL.”1 2. This phrase was again used in Hawaii on January 13, 2018. At 8:07 a.m. Hawaii Standard Time (HST), on-duty warning officers of the State of Hawaii Emergency Management Agency (HI-EMA) sought to conduct an internal exercise of their ballistic missile defense drill using the Emergency Alert System (EAS) and Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA).2 The exercise went awry, resulting in HI-EMA sending the following message throughout Hawaii: BALLISTIC MISSILE THREAT INBOUND TO HAWAII. SEEK IMMEDIATE SHELTER. THIS IS NOT A DRILL.3 3. This false emergency alert resulted in 38 minutes of confusion, fear and uncertainty for the residents of Hawaii.4 Although some suspected that the alert was a mistake, in part due to the absence of air-raid sirens, and made calls or checked social media to confirm the alert’s authenticity,5 for many Hawaiians, the false alert created the expectation that a missile strike could be only minutes away. According to the Bureau’s investigation, it took HI-EMA until 8:20 a.m.

data.summary: Seoul Metropolitan Government is sending an Actual, Extreme air-raid alert to all of Seoul (KR-ADM 11). The area requested for this event is Baengnyeong-myeon and Daecheong-myeon, Ongjin-gun, Incheon (KR-ADM 28720), which is the area in the Ministry's active alert. Seoul is not registered for that area, so the drafter cannot simply retarget the alert. Sending it to Seoul would also extend a higher authority's air-raid alert to a city that authority did not cover. A person, together with the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, must decide whether this alert goes out at all.

objections.issue: The alert's target area (all of Seoul, KR-ADM 11) does not match the area requested for this event (Ongjin-gun, Incheon, KR-ADM 28720). Seoul's register entry covers only KR-ADM=11 and the Seoul polygon, so Seoul cannot cover the requested area either.
objections.fix: Do not send for Seoul. A person must confirm which authority should alert KR-ADM 28720 (the Ministry already has). Seoul may issue only if a Seoul-specific threat is separately confirmed and an area is requested for it.

evidence.quote: Baengnyeong-myeon and Daecheong-myeon, Ongjin-gun, Incheon (area named in the ministry's alert)
The text describing the affected area of the alert message

objections.issue: A level-2 local authority is issuing an Actual, Extreme air-raid alert that overreaches the active level-1 Ministry air-raid alert. The Ministry's alert covers only KR-ADM 28720, and this alert extends it to the whole of Seoul without the higher authority's decision.
objections.fix: Hold the alert. Get a decision from the Ministry of the Interior and Safety (level 1) on whether Seoul is under threat before any air-raid alert is sent to Seoul.
